study type: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis with a nested case-control study
cohort: Women giving birth at the National Maternal and Child Health Centre (NMCHC) in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, from 2017 to 2020
finding: The study found that stillbirth rates increased between 2017 and 2020, and identified maternal age, prematurity, SGA, breech/transverse births, history of abnormal vaginal discharge, and history of stillbirth as independent risk factors for stillbirth, while caesarean section was found to reduce the odds of stillbirth.
mod_finding: Caesarean section reduced the likelihood of having a stillborn baby by about half.
